hero.filename: USS Selfridge (DD-357) fitted with temporary bow, 24 January 1944 (80-G-316295).jpg
hero.caption: The U.S. Navy destroyer USS Selfridge (DD-357) upon arrival at the Mare Island Naval Shipyard, California (USA), on 24 January 1944. She lost her bow after a torpedo hit during the Battle of Vella Lavella on 6 October 1943. A temporary bow was fittet at Tulagi and Noumea so that she could reach the U.S. West Coast for permanent repairs.

images.filename: USS Selfridge and OBannon damaged Oct 1943.JPG
images.caption: The U.S. Navy destroyers USS Selfridge (DD-357), left, and USS O'Bannon (DD-450) damaged at Noumea, Espiritu Santo, after the naval Battle of Vella Lavella, on 7 October 1943. Selfridge´s bow was torn off by a Japanese torpedo (note sailors climbing in the wrecked gun turret). O'Bannon collided with USS Chevalier (DD-451) during the battle, after Chevalier had been hit by a torpedo (she had to be sunk later).
